title: Control tapestry notebook — SOC2 quick-threads
content:
Purpose and state: quick, messy scratchpad for mapping obvious controls to evidence we can reasonably collect before the next SOC2 checkpoint. Not a finished control narrative — more a set of provable evidence candidates + owners + open questions. Use to seed a formal control file later.

High-level goals
- Capture low-effort/high-confidence evidence first (logs, backups, IAM changes)
- Identify gaps that require engineering work (automations, retention, tooling)
- Create minimal owner + ask per item so we can parallelize evidence collection

Context notes (why some items matter)
- Hosted API + Dedicated + Private create different evidence surfaces: hosted telemetry vs customer-managed logs. We need control language that covers all three environments without overclaiming.
- Focus on change control, access reviews, key management, backup & restore proofs, and incident timelines — those keep coming up on past audits.

Quick mapping (SOC2 criteria -> candidate evidence -> owner -> notes)
- CC:Change Management -> PR + release tagging + rollback runbook -> owner: Platform Eng (Keita) -> evidence: GitHub PR history for release-x, CI artifact hashes, canary rollout logs. TODO: ask Release Eng to export canary rollback events for Jan–Mar.
- CC:Logical Access -> IAM audit + MFA enforcement -> owner: SRE (Maya) -> evidence: IAM policy snapshots, auth provider (Okta) reports, MFA enforcement policy. Open question: do service-to-service tokens count as "user" access? Add doc note.
- CC:Encryption/KMS -> KMS key rotation + access logs -> owner: Infra (Ramon) -> evidence: KMS rotation schedule, Cloud KMS access logs, HSM attestations if used in Private installs. Note: Private customers may use their KMS; we need a template question set for them.
- CC:Availability/Backups -> backup jobs + restore drills -> owner: Storage Ops -> evidence: snapshots, S3 lifecycle policies, last successful restore test (date & scope). TODO: schedule a small restore test for a non-prod cluster before 2026-03-20.
- CC:Monitoring/Alerting -> incident timelines + postmortems -> owner: Observability (Meghan) -> evidence: PagerDuty incidents, Opsgenie alerts, postmortem docs. Need to tag which incidents relate to production vs test.

Evidence harvesting checklist (practical steps)
- Pull IAM configuration export (Okta + GCP/AWS) — Maya
- Export KMS access logs (last 12 months) — Ramon (request with infra-support ticket)
- Compile list of release tags and associated deploy diffs for past 6 months — Keita
- Collect last 3 restore/drill records and the associated tickets — Storage Ops
- Aggregate a short set (3–5) of postmortems demonstrating incident response times and follow-through — Observability
- Short screenshots/queries for egress firewall rules for Private customers — Solutions Eng (ask for template)

Open questions / action items (ranked)
- Q1: What retention length do auditors expect for auth logs vs KMS logs? (ask external auditor) — HIGH priority
- Q2: For Dedicated capacity customers, can we assert Redwood-managed backups? Need to separate claims for dedicated-hosted vs private installs. — MED priority
- Q3: Are ephemeral service tokens considered an access method requiring rotation evidence? Decide a policy. — MED
- A1: Create a single-page template to request KMS evidence from Private customers (fields: key IDs, rotation schedule, audit logs export instructions). Owner: Solutions Eng.

Rough risk matrix (quick eyeball)
- High risk (requires engineering): lack of automated backup verification, missing KMS access logs for Private installs, no documented release rollback.
- Medium risk (process/policy): irregular access review cadence, incomplete postmortems.
- Low risk (easy evidence): screenshots of MFA enforcement, exportable IAM role lists, simple S3 bucket lifecycle configs.

Notes for auditors / narrative pointers (very informal)
- We should avoid technical deep-dives in the control statement; point to artifacts and a short "how we check" list. Eg: "Access reviews performed quarterly; artifacts: Okta report export (dates), Slack approval threads, and the quarterly access review ticket (TSK-4127)".
- For Private customers: include a standard paragraph that says "customer-managed KMS may be used; Redwood can provide guidance and request logs as part of onboarding" — don't overpromise.

Sample checklist entry (template to copy into formal evidence doc)
- Control: MFA enforced for all human access to prod console
  - Evidence: Okta policy screenshot (2026-02-02), sysadmin user list export (CSV), one sample MFA login event (timestamp)
  - Owner: Maya Lin
  - Status: collected (place link to export)

Misc quick snippets / one-liners to transplant into formal docs
- "Release rollouts are tracked via GitHub tags and an internal rollout ID; canary rollbacks are recorded in the release-runbooks S3 prefix."
- "Key rotation is performed annually; ad-hoc rotations are logged in Cloud KMS admin logs and attached to the rotation ticket."
- "Private deployments: customer KMS and logging may be used; Redwood requests exportable audit logs during onboarding and retains a hashed proof of receipt in the customer folder."

Communication plan for next two weeks
- This doc -> convert into a short Confluence checklist for auditors (owner: Jora) by 2026-03-10
- Raid key evidence items via direct asks (Maya/Ramon/Keita) and collect artifacts into a shared drive folder -> target 2026-03-17
- Draft one control narrative for Change Management + three artifacts and circulate to Security for review -> target 2026-03-22

Quick links / tickets to follow up
- TSK-4127 (access review cadence follow-up)
- infra-support/req-889 (KMS logs export)
- github/infra#238 (ssh-audit PR reference mentioned above)

Random scratch ideas to consider later
- Automate a weekly mini-evidence bundle: small zip containing key JSON exports (Okta, KMS meta, last snapshot manifest) and a checksum file — store in retention-labeled bucket. Could dramatically reduce auditor dragging.
- Lightweight "proof-of-restore" job that runs monthly on a non-prod partition and auto-creates a ticket with logs and artifacts.

End notes (brain-dump):
- Keep control language narrow and defensible. Don't claim we do things we only do sometimes. If it's "sometimes" then make it a documented exception with mitigation steps.
- This doc will be the source for a few tickets — tag TSKs in next update.

-- Jora

(If anything here is already tracked in Confluence or an existing ticket, crosslink it back; this is intentionally lightweight and messy so we can move quickly.)
